re optional and fall back to suite defaults |\n| `POST .../eval-runs` | Create a run from a `suiteId` (rerun; `serverIds` optional
, defaults to the suite's saved servers) or `suiteName` + inline `tests` + `serverIds` (new suite). `environmentId` (requires `sui
teId`) runs against one of the suite's attached environments instead. Responds `202` + `runId` |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteI
d}` | Edit suite settings, including `environmentIds` (the project environments the suite runs against (non-empty array sets/repla
ces, `null` clears) |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/schedule` | Enable/disable scheduled runs; `environmentId` pins which en
vironment they launch |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` | Run status, result, and summary; poll until terminal. Carries `gateWaiver
`: the audited override in force over this run's gate, or `null` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate` | The stored suite quality-
gate report for this run (`passed` / `failed` / `non_gateable` / `not_configured`). `not_configured` is a 200 report, never a miss
ing route |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/decision-summary` | **Start here when a run did not pass.** The canonical run decision c
ontract: the verdict and where it came from, counts labelled with the population they count, the run's own verdict decision, and p
er-trial diagnostics with the user-value chain, the first failed stage, the failure category, evidence scoped to that stage, and o
ne next action (paginated) |\n| `POST .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | Override a **failing** run's release gate until `expir
esAt` (required, future, max 30 days out), with a `reason` (required, max 500 chars). Manage tier. Does NOT change the run's `resu
lt`; the run keeps its verdict and the waiver is reported alongside it. `409` when one is already in force, returning the existing
waiver |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | The waiver in force over a run, or `null`. Readable by anyone who can view
the run |\n| `DELETE .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers/{waiverId}` | Revoke a waiver, putting the gate back. Idempotent; a secon
d call reports the original revocation rather than restamping it |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations` | Per-iteration resul
ts: tool calls, token usage, latency (paginated) |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations/{iterationId}/trace` | Full trace: mes

sages + expected-vs-actual analysis |
| `GET .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/runs` | Recent runs for a suite, newest first |

**Eval
result ingestion** (`/projects/{projectId}/eval-ingest/...`): how `@mcpjam/sdk` saves results from eval runs executed outside the
platform (local dev, CI). The `{projectId}` segment accepts the literal `default` for the key org's Default project. Most users ne
ver call these directly; set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` and the [SDK reporter](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/concepts/saving-results.md) does:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-ingest/report` | One-shot: create a run from finished results and fin
alize it |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/start` | Chunked flow: create (or idempotently reuse) a run by `externalRunId` |\n| `POST
.../eval-ingest/runs/iterations` | Append an iteration batch to a started run |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/finalize` | Finaliz
e a chunked run (idempotent) |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` | Store one artifact's raw bytes (widget HTML too large to send
inline) and return its `storageId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts/upload-url` | Retired. Answers `410 Gone` with `details.c
ode: \"SDK_UPGRADE_REQUIRED\"`. `@mcpjam/sdk` 8.17.0 and later upload artifacts with `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` instead |\n\

n**Agent** (`/projects/{projectId}/agent`): a headless assistant turn for
building conversational surfaces:

| Endpoint | What
it does |\n| - | - |\n| `POST .../agent` | Run ONE assistant turn over a `messages` history (`{role: \"user\"\\|\"assistant\", con
tent}` items, max 50 messages × 8 KB each, 96 KB total). The model is pinned server-side and billed to the project. The turn can r
ead project servers/suites/runs and **create eval suites**; it can NOT start runs: kick those off yourself with `POST .../eval-run
s`. Responds synchronously with `reply`, the `toolCalls` it made, `createdResources` (ids + app links), and token `usage`. Capped
at 4 concurrent turns per organization and \\~90 s wall clock. **Not idempotent; never blind-retry**: dedupe on your own trigger i
dentity, and on an error response check `details.createdResources` (and, after a lost response, list suites) before retrying, or y

ou'll create duplicates |

**Studies** (`/projects/{projectId}/studies...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .
../studies` | List the project's published studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId
}` | One study's full read: model, system prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environment it publishes, and its in
sights envelope. The last two need workspace membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, never null |\n\n**Swarms, aut
horing** (`/projects/{projectId}/personas...`, `.../goals...`,\n`.../swarms...`): the definitions a swarm run executes. A **person
a** is a\nreusable synthetic character; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a\n**swarm** is an authoring container holding de

faults for the goals made
under it. Nothing here starts anything; launching is
`POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs`.

| Endpoint | W

hat it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../personas` | List the project's personas |
| `POST .../personas` | Create a persona (accepts
`Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../personas/{personaId}` | One persona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{personaId}` | Update a persona. Goa
ls reference it by id, so renaming is safe |\n| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. **409** while goals still re
ference it |\n| `GET .../goals` | List the project's goals |\n| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `per
sonaId` and `swarmId` must be in this project |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PATCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a
goal. `null` CLEARS `environmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |\n| `DELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archi
ve** a goal; existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed |\n| `GET .../swarms` | List swarm containers |\n| `POST
.../swarms` | Create a swarm container (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | One swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swa
rms/{swarmId}` | Update the container's defaults. Not a cascade; existing goals keep their own values |\n| `DELETE .../swarms/{swa
rmId}` | **Archive** a swarm. The goals under it stay launchable |\n\n**Swarms, generation**. Drafts a model writes for you. Both
routes return\ncandidates and **persist nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create\nroutes above. Neither accepts an `Ide

mpotency-Key`, and retries return
different drafts.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../personas/generate` | D
raft a slate of personas (and goals for each) grounded in a server attachment or an environment |\n| `POST .../goals/generate` | D

raft goals for a persona passed **by value**, so you can draft before you save |

> [!WARNING]
>
> The generation routes consu
me **no customer credits** (the model cost is on\n> MCPJam). They are still subject to usage limits, and each limit means a\n> dif
ferent wait: a per-minute burst brake (`429`, retry in seconds), your\n> organization's daily generation quota (`429`, resets at U
TC midnight), and\n> MCPJam's own daily budget for the feature (`429` with\n> `details.code: \"platform_capacity\"`, resets at UTC
midnight). All three carry\n> `Retry-After`. Honor it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `false`\n> on every one: buying

credits does not lift them, so do not retry in a loop
> or switch identities to get around them.

**Swarms, runs** (`/projects

/{projectId}/goals/{goalId}/runs`,
`.../goal-runs/...`): launching a goal and reading what it produced:

| Endpoint | What it d

oes |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | That goal's runs, newest first |
| `POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | **Launch.
** Answers `202`; the fan-out has started, not finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expectedSponsored` is how many conversa
tions you expect MCPJam to sponsor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_funding_changed`) and nothing is cre
